reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getNextDate and adds shared predicates (isDailyWeekendSkip, isNonBusinessDay), but the new range handler and getUpcomingDates recompose the skip-or-move rule themselves instead of sharing one occurrence-to-final-day function.

duplication.why: The 'filter daily non-business days, then move weekend/holiday days when skipWeekend' pipeline is written out in getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and (as a branch) getNextDate, and schedule-template keeps its own skipWeekend ? adjust : date wrapper.

placement.why: Date rules live in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in server/schedules/app.ts as the tree does; the rule composition leaking into each server caller is the weak point.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedules, the template engine, rule parsing and the type; the release note and tests are expected, nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: Workable, but the noSkipWeekend flag of getNextDate now also switches daily skipping, lookahead/padding heuristics are magic numbers, and changing the rule again means editing three or four call sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and budget/schedule-template.ts getAdjustedDate, apply the daily-skip/move decision themselves rather than through getNextDate or a single shared adjust function.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' filter(isDailyWeekendSkip/isNonBusinessDay) + map(getDateWithSkippedWeekend) chain with the predicate inlined differently; schedule-template wraps the same ternary in a local getAdjustedDate closure.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a skipDailyWeekends special-case branch and its noSkipWeekend flag is overloaded by schedule-template; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's getAdjustedDate each re-implement the skip-or-move composition.
